title: vi, Emacs, and the Editor Wars (1976)
explainer: The two editor lineages behind much of what you're installing in this lesson both trace back to 1976: Bill Joy wrote vi at UC Berkeley as a full-screen 'visual' mode on top of a line editor called ex, while Richard Stallman and Guy Steele built the first Emacs out of a tangle of TECO editing macros at MIT around the same time. The decades-long, good-natured 'editor wars' between their descendants (Vim and GNU Emacs) are really a proxy fight between two different philosophies of text editing - modal commands versus chorded keystrokes - that predate nearly every other tool in this course.
